questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:
questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs like speed limit signs are usually rectangular. They are white with black lettering or symbols. You must follow the rules shown on these signs.

questions.question: When traveling in a group, riders should:

options.text: Spread out to make the group easier to see.
Stay close together to make the group easier to see.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay close together to make the group easier to see.
questions.explanation: Riders in a group should stay close together while leaving room to maneuver safely. This makes the group easier to see and prevents riders from becoming separated. Riding in pairs does not give enough room to move safely.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a good safety tip?

options.text: Slow to a safe speed before turning.
When turning, lean in the direction you wish to go.
Avoid dragging your feet on the roadway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid looking at other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Slow down before you turn and lean in the direction of the turn. Do not drag your feet on the road—they could catch on something and cause you to lose control. Always watch for other traffic.

questions.question: The effects of marijuana consumption can last for:
questions.correctAnswerText: More than six hours.
questions.explanation: Smoked marijuana starts to affect the user within minutes and lasts for two to four hours. Eaten marijuana takes over an hour to start working but can affect the person for more than six hours.

questions.question: How does the stopping distance for motorcycles compare to the stopping distance for cars?

options.text: Cars need much longer to stop.
Cars need a little longer to stop.
Both motorcycles and cars take about the same amount of time to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both motorcycles and cars take about the same amount of time to stop.
questions.explanation: Under normal conditions, motorcycles and cars stop in about the same distance. However, wet or slippery pavement makes it much harder for motorcycles to stop quickly.

questions.question: When riding under normal conditions, maintain a minimum following distance of:
questions.correctAnswerText: Four seconds.
questions.explanation: Keep at least four seconds of distance between you and the vehicle ahead under normal conditions. Increase this distance when conditions are not ideal.

questions.question: Which of the following is a poor reason to sound your horn?

options.text: A driver in the lane next to you is too close to the vehicle ahead of them.
A parked car has a person in the driver's seat.
You want people to look at your motorcycle.
You are passing someone who is in the street.

questions.correctAnswerText: You want people to look at your motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Sound your horn before passing a vehicle or pedestrian who might move into your lane. If a driver is following too closely to the car ahead, they may try to cut in front of you. Use your horn when passing someone in a parked car, a pedestrian, or a bicyclist on the street. Do not use your horn just to get attention for your motorcycle.

questions.question: Your lane position should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Increase your ability to see and be seen.
Prevent access to an escape route.

questions.correctAnswerText: Prevent access to an escape route.
questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you see others and be seen. It keeps you away from wind blasts, blind spots, and road hazards. Your position should keep other drivers from sharing your lane and should give you a way to escape if a hazard appears.

questions.question: When looking through a turn, you should:

options.text: Turn both your head and your shoulders to get a better look.
Turn just your head, not your shoulders.
Only move your eyes, not your head.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn just your head, not your shoulders.
questions.explanation: Look through the turn to see where you want to go. Turn just your head, keep your shoulders still, and look straight ahead at the horizon.

questions.question: A front tire blowout is especially dangerous because:

options.text: The front part of the motorcycle will be lower than usual.
The rear brake cannot be used.
The front brake cannot be used.

questions.correctAnswerText: It affects the steering.
questions.explanation: A front tire blowout is very dangerous because it makes steering difficult. You will notice your steering become heavy if your front tire has blown out.

questions.question: If your rear wheel locks while braking, what should you do?

options.text: Release the brake until the rear tire grips again, then brake again.
Release the brake and use only the front brake.
Keep the brake locked until the motorcycle stops.
Release the brake and coast to a stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the brake locked until the motorcycle stops.
questions.explanation: If your rear wheel locks while braking, do not release the brake. Keep it locked until you stop completely.

questions.question: When riding in a group, what should you do?

options.text: Put inexperienced riders at the back of the group.
Keep safe distance between you and other riders.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep safe distance between you and other riders.
questions.explanation: When riding in a group, use a staggered formation. Check your mirrors often. Experienced riders should lead and sweep. Always keep proper space between riders.

questions.question: How many motorcycle and car crashes happen because a car driver fails to give the motorcycle the right-of-way?
questions.correctAnswerText: Over 50 percent
questions.explanation: Over half of all crashes between motorcycles and cars happen because car drivers fail to give the motorcycle the right-of-way.

questions.question: How do you swerve correctly on a motorcycle?

options.text: Push the handle grip in the direction you want to go.
Push the handle grip in the opposite direction you want to go.

questions.correctAnswerText: Push the handle grip in the direction you want to go.
questions.explanation: To swerve, push the handle grip in the direction you want to go. To swerve left, push the left grip, then the right to straighten out. To swerve right, push the right grip, then the left.

questions.question: What color vest or jacket helps you be seen best?
questions.correctAnswerText: Red
questions.explanation: Wear bright colors to be seen. Bright red, orange, yellow, or green are best. Avoid dark or dull colors.

questions.question: What does this hand signal mean?

options.text: Line up in a single file.

questions.correctAnswerText: Line up in a single file.
questions.explanation: When the lead rider raises their left arm with one finger up, it means the group should form a single-file line.

questions.question: When is it most important to flash your brake light?

options.text: When you need to slow down suddenly.
When a stop sign is ahead.
When your turn signals don't work.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you need to slow down suddenly.
questions.explanation: Flash your brake light before slowing down suddenly, especially if a rider is following too closely. This warns them about hazards ahead that you are avoiding.

questions.question: To carry a passenger safely, you may need to adjust:
questions.correctAnswerText: The shocks.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight, so adjust the shocks. Also adjust the headlight and mirrors because the motorcycle will sit at a different angle.

questions.question: When packing items on a motorcycle, where should heavier items go?
questions.correctAnswerText: Toward the front.
questions.explanation: Pack heavier items toward the front. Load everything over or in front of the rear axle. Put lighter items behind you.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning sign
questions.explanation: Yellow signs with black lettering or symbols are warning signs. They tell you about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: Do motorcycle windshields protect your eyes?

options.text: Yes, they work as well as a face shield.
Yes, they work as well as goggles.
No, they do not protect your eyes from the wind.
No, they do not protect against objects thrown from other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, they do not protect your eyes from the wind.
questions.explanation: A windshield is not a good replacement for a face shield or goggles. Most windshields do not protect your eyes from the wind.

questions.question: When carrying a heavy load on your motorcycle, what should you adjust?
questions.correctAnswerText: Suspension.
questions.explanation: Before riding with a heavy load, check your tire pressure, spring pre-load, air shocks, and dampers. Set them to the manufacturer's recommended settings for the added weight.

questions.question: A rider wearing a helmet is how many times more likely to survive a crash?
questions.correctAnswerText: Three times
questions.explanation: Riders without helmets are three times more likely to die from head injuries in a crash than riders wearing helmets.

questions.question: The center of a lane often has an oily strip. When is this area unsafe for motorcyclists?

options.text: It is usually safe, but not when the road is wet.
It is usually safe, but not when it is sunny.
It is always safe no matter the weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is usually safe, but not when the road is wet.
questions.explanation: Oil from cars collects in a strip in the center of the lane. This area is usually safe for motorcyclists unless the road is wet. The strip is usually about two feet wide, so you can often ride to one side of it and still be in the center part of the lane.

questions.question: What should you do with your head when riding through a turn?

options.text: Turn your head and shoulders to look through the turn.
Keep your knees away from the gas tank.
Turn only your head and eyes to look through the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn only your head and eyes to look through the turn.
questions.explanation: When turning, look toward where you want to go. Turn only your head, not your shoulders, and keep your eyes level with the horizon.
